newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal students blockade roads.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal students blockade roads.

text.p: Tribal students in the southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts have blockaded roads, damaged cars and stabbed travellers in protest against alleged harassment by Bengali-speaking settlers, police said on Tuesday.
"The road communications between Khagrachari and the rest of the country have been snapped since Monday due to the blockade by the tribal students," said one police officer.
Police said to enforce their blockade, the students were demonstrating on approach roads around Khagrachari town.

The students burnt a motorcycle, damaged two other vehicles and stabbed two bus passengers on Monday. They also attacked a peace procession by the settlers at Khagrachari town, wounding five people on Monday.
Police said the protest was over an attack last week on tribal villagers by settlers angered by an earlier assault on a Bengali for alleged pickpocketing.
Police said efforts by the local administration to calm the protesters had so far failed.

The tribal insurgency began in 1973 in the 5,500 square-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, which border India and Burma. More than 8,500 people have been killed in the violence, according to official figures.
The tribal insurgents, called Shanti Bahini, want political autonomy for the Hill Tracts and the expulsion from the region of the Bengali settlers, something Bangladesh has rejected.
